newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia plans sale of mobile phone firm stake.
newsitem.headline: Latvia plans sale of mobile phone firm stake.

text.p: The Latvian government plans to sell its stake in the sole mobile phone operator, Latvijas Mobilais Telefons (LMT), the government press office said on Monday.

It said in a statement that the government cabinet's economics and finance committee approved a draft law on selling the state's share of LMT. The committee's recommendations are usually approved by the full cabinet.
The state owns 51 percent of LMT, currently the sole operator of NMT and GSM mobile phone services. A second operator, Baltel, is in the process of being setting up.
The remaining 49 percent of LMT is owned by Telecom Finland and Sweden's Telia.
Telecom Finland also owns a stake in majority state-owned telecommunications firm Lattelekom along with Britain's Cable and Wireless.
